summary: Petition under Section 79 (1) (k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 19(3) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2024 seeking extension of infirm power injection and Regulation 57 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations. - _f.Grant an extension for injection of infirm power to the Petitioner for the purpose of charging and initiating trial run of the balance 13.2 MW (i.e., 4 WTGs- NKT 14, NKT19, NKT-76, NKT-77) for its Project connected to Bhuj-PS;_ - _g.Declare and hold that the delay in charging and completion of trial run of the aforesaid Wind Turbine Generator was caused due to circumstances beyond the control of the Petitioner;_ The Petitioner has also made the following interim prayers vide the instant Petition: - _a.The Petitioner respectfully prays that this Hon’ble Commission may be pleased to pass the following interim directions: Direct Western Regional_ - (a) The Petitioner is the developer of a 100 MW installed capacity Hybrid (92.4 MW Wind and 37.5 MW Solar) Project at Village Devasar, Taluka Nakhatrana and District Kutch, Gujarat, having connectivity to ISTS at Bhuj PS, Gujarat, for supply of 100 MW Round-the-Clock power on captive basis to Hindalco Industries Ltd., for a period of 25 years from the commissioning date. - (e) The commissioning of the 4 WTGs was prevented by multiple unforeseen events, as under, which were beyond the Petitioner’s control: - ➢ From 06.07.2025 onwards, the Petitioner encountered severe and recurring right-of-way (RoW) obstructions at various locations along the evacuation system associated with the subject WTGs. Local **3.** During the hearing, Petitioner briefly outlined the facts of the case, as already submitted in the main Petition. After hearing the Parties, the Commission admitted the Petition and directed the Parties to file, on affidavit, the detailed reasons for the non-completion of the trial run and the commissioning of the part capacity after obtaining FTC approval for the same and details of FTC approval and infirm power injection extension by WRLDC within one week. **4.** Petitioner, in compliance with the ROP for hearing dated 24.02.2026, vide affidavit dated 05.03.2026, has made the following submissions: - (c) Petitioner was required to approach this Commission at least 15 days in advance of the completion of the stipulated period, i.e., on or before 30.09.2026; however, the Petition was filed on 11.02.2026. The delay of 133 days in filing the present Petition was neither intentional nor attributable to any negligence, but was occasioned entirely due to circumstances beyond its control. - (h) Owing to the force majeure circumstances detailed above, the Petitioner, vide letter dated 31.07.2025, sought extension of trial run timelines up to 15.10.2025. Considering the reasons furnished, the Respondent vide letter dated 01.08.2025 granted extension up to 15.10.2025. However, due to reasons detailed above, the Petitioner could not complete the trial run of the remaining 4 WTGs within the extended timeline. The Petitioner, by way of a letter dated 05.10.2025, requested the Respondent for further extension for the trial run till 21.11.2025. However, any further extension beyond 24.11.2025 for infirm power injection is subject to the approval of this Commission in terms of Regulation 19 of the Grid Code. **5.** During the hearing, Petitioner reiterated the facts of the case and informed the Commission that it had made submissions in compliance with the directions vide RoP dated 24.02.2026. The representative of the Respondent, WRLDC, submitted that it has no objection to the matter and that the Commission may pass an Order as deemed fit. Considering this, the Commission reserved the matter for Order. - of infirm power and condone the delay of 133 days in filing the instant Petition by exercising the power to relax. **11.** We have perused the submissions of the Petitioner and the information on record. The issues that arise for our consideration are as under: - **2) Whether the Petitioner can be granted an extension of time for the injection of infirm power?** _The Commission, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by an affected person to remove the hardship arising out of the operation of any of these regulations, applicable to a class of persons.”_ **13.** Petitioner was required to approach this Commission at least 15 days in advance of the completion of the stipulated period, i.e. on or before 30.09.2025, as the latest extension for injection of infirm power by the WRLDC was valid up to 15.10.2025. However, the petition was filed on 11.02.2026, after a delay of about 133 days. Petitioner has submitted that the delay in filing the present Petition was neither intentional nor attributable to any negligence, but was occasioned entirely due to force majeure-like circumstances beyond its control. **14.** Further, Petitioner has submitted the following reasons for the non-completion of trial run and commissioning activities related to the pending WTGs: **17.** As discussed above, we condone the delay in filing the Petition and allow the Petitioner under Regulation 19(3) of the 2023 Grid Code an extension of the period for interchange of power, latest up to 20 days from the date of issuance of this Order. Petitioner is directed to complete all commissioning activities related to the project capacity under the instant Petition within the allowed period. The events impacted the commissioning activities, which are acknowledged only to allow extension of infirm power injection under Regulation 19(3) of the 2023 Grid Code, not otherwise.
